questions.question: Which country’s authorities were flagged by India in 2025 for hybrid cannabis smuggling via couriers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thailand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In early **2025**, Indian drug law enforcement agencies, led by the **Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB)**, flagged **Thailand** as a major source of **hybrid cannabis** being smuggled into the country.
 
• The illicit trade primarily utilizes international **courier services** and the **postal network** to deliver high-potency cannabis "buds" to major Indian metropolitan areas such as **Mumbai**, **Delhi**, and **Bengaluru**.
 
• **Hybrid cannabis** from **Thailand** is specifically targeted due to its high **THC (Tetrahydrocannabinol)** content, which ranges between **15% to 30%**, making it far more potent and expensive than the locally grown variety.
 
• Authorities noted that smugglers often use sophisticated **vacuum-sealed packaging** to evade detection by **K-9 units** and conceal the drugs inside harmless items like **clothing**, **food containers**, or **electronics**. ***Hence, Thailand is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Decriminalization in Thailand**:
 
 
• **Thailand** became the first country in **Asia** to decriminalize cannabis in **June 2022**. This move led to a proliferation of cannabis dispensaries across cities like **Bangkok** and **Phuket**.
 
• While intended for medical and domestic economic growth, the lack of stringent export regulations initially allowed **hybrid strains** to be diverted into the international **black market**.
 
 
 
• **NDPS Act, 1985**:
 
 
• In **India**, cannabis is regulated under the **Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985**.
 
• The law strictly prohibits the **production, sale, and consumption** of the flowering or fruiting tops (ganja) and the separated resin (charas) of the cannabis plant.
 
• Offenses involving "commercial quantities" of these substances can lead to rigorous imprisonment of **10 to 20 years**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**:
 
 
• The street value of **Thai hybrid cannabis** in **India** is significantly higher than indigenous varieties, often retailing between **₹2,000 and ₹5,000 per gram**.
 
• This high profit margin has incentivized organized **criminal syndicates** to establish robust courier-based supply chains between **Southeast Asia** and **South Asia**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Surveillance**: To counter this trend in **2025**, the **Customs Department** and the **NCB** have increased the deployment of **Advanced X-ray Baggage Inspection Systems (AXIS)** and **AI-based profiling** at international courier terminals.
 
• **International Cooperation**: **India** has engaged in bilateral discussions with **Thailand** to strengthen **intelligence sharing** and monitor the bulk purchase of cannabis by foreign nationals to prevent **transnational smuggling**.
 
• **Health Risks**: Health experts warn that **hybrid cannabis** with extreme **THC levels** can lead to severe **psychological issues**, including **paranoia** and **cannabis-induced psychosis**, particularly among the youth in urban centers.

questions.question: According to the Union Budget 2025–26, how many new Day Care Cancer Centres will be set up in district hospitals in 2025–26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**200**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the presentation of the **Union Budget 2025–26**, Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** announced the establishment of **200** new **Day Care Cancer Centres** across **district hospitals** in the country.
 
• The initiative is designed to decentralize **oncology services**, bringing critical cancer care closer to the homes of patients residing in **rural** and **semi-urban areas**.
 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** was presented in the **Parliament** on **February 1, 2025**, outlining several health-centric measures to improve the **quality of life** and **longevity** of citizens.
 
• These centres will primarily cater to patients requiring **chemotherapy** and **palliative care**, eliminating the need for long-distance travel to **metropolitan tertiary care hospitals**.
 
• By setting up these facilities at the **district level**, the government aims to address the rising burden of **non-communicable diseases (NCDs)**, particularly **cancer**, which has seen a significant spike in incidence rates in **India**.
 
• This step is aligned with the vision of **Universal Health Coverage (UHC)** and strengthening the **public healthcare delivery system** through the **National Health Mission (NHM)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 200.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concept of Day Care Cancer Centres:**

 
 
• A **Day Care Cancer Centre** is a specialized facility where medical procedures such as **chemotherapy**, **blood transfusions**, and **targeted therapy** are performed within a few hours.
 
• Patients are admitted and discharged on the **same day**, which significantly reduces **hospitalization costs** and frees up beds for surgical or emergency cases.
 
• These centres provide a comfortable environment for patients to receive **non-surgical treatment** while staying close to their support systems.
 
 
 
• **Healthcare in Union Budget 2025–26:**
 
 
• The **2025–26 budget** emphasized **Social Justice** and **Human Resource Development** as key pillars for India's growth.
 
• The allocation for the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)** saw a strategic increase to bolster **primary** and **secondary healthcare** infrastructure.
 
• The focus remains on enhancing the **digital health ecosystem** and expanding the reach of **Ayushman Bharat** schemes.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Cancer Care in India:**
 
 
• According to the **Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)**, the number of cancer cases in **India** is projected to rise to **15.7 lakh** by **2025**.
 
• High **out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE)** often leads to patients dropping out of treatment; the **200** new centres are expected to mitigate this financial risk for **low-income families**.
 
• Early detection and regular **follow-up cycles**, which are crucial for survival, will become more manageable with localized centres.
 
 
 
• **Other Health Initiatives:**
 
 
• The government continues to promote the **Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)**, which provides health insurance of **Rs. 5 lakh** per family.
 
• There is a continuous effort to increase the number of **All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS)** and **medical colleges** to improve the **doctor-to-patient ratio**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** has identified **9 priorities** for the government, including **Health and Social Security**.
 
• The **200 Day Care Cancer Centres** will be integrated with the **National Digital Health Mission (NDHM)** to maintain **Electronic Health Records (EHR)** for cancer patients.
 
• This initiative is expected to create **employment opportunities** for specialized **oncology nurses**, **medical technicians**, and **counselors** at the district level.
 
• By decentralizing care, the government hopes to reduce the massive footfall at **regional cancer centres** like **Tata Memorial Hospital** or **AIIMS New Delhi**, allowing those institutions to focus on complex **research and surgeries**.

questions.question: Which Indian footballer received the Padma Shri in 2025 for his contributions to the sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IM Vijayan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inivalappil Mani Vijayan**, popularly known as **IM Vijayan**, is a legendary former captain of the **Indian national football team**.
 
• In **2025**, the Government of India announced the **Padma Shri**, the country's **fourth-highest civilian award**, for **IM Vijayan** in recognition of his exceptional contribution to **Indian football**.
 
• Hailing from **Thrissur, Kerala**, he is often referred to by the nickname **"Kalo Harin"** (Black Buck) due to his incredible speed, poaching ability, and technical skills on the field.
 
• He was one of the most prolific goal-scorers for India during the **1990s** and early **2000s**, forming a famous attacking partnership with **Bhaichung Bhutia**.
 
• **IM Vijayan** was the first player to be named the **AIFF Player of the Year** three times, achieving this feat in **1993, 1997, and 1999**.
 
• Before receiving the Padma Shri, he was honored with the **Arjuna Award** in **2003** for his outstanding achievements in national sports.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is IM Vijayan__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhaichung Bhutia:**

 
 
• Known as the **"Sikkimese Sniper"**, he is a former Indian captain and the first Indian footballer to sign a professional contract with a **European club** (**Bury FC** in England).
 
• He received the **Padma Shri** in **2008** and the **Arjuna Award** in **1998**.
 
 
 
• **Sunil Chhetri:**
 
 
• He is the **all-time leading goal-scorer** for the Indian national team and currently ranks among the top international goal-scorers globally.
 
• Chhetri was awarded the **Padma Shri** in **2019** and became the first footballer to receive the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in **2021**.
 
 
 
• **Sandesh Jhingan:**
 
 
• A prominent **central defender** for the Indian national team, he received the **Arjuna Award** in **2020**. He has been a mainstay in the Indian defense for several years.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards:**
 
 
• The **Padma Awards** were instituted in **1954** and are announced every year on the eve of **Republic Day** (**January 26**).
 
• The awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (distinguished service of high order), and **Padma Shri** (distinguished service).
 
• The **President of India** confers these awards at a formal ceremony held at **Rashtrapati Bhavan**, usually around **March or April**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IM Vijayan's Career Highlights:** He scored one of the **fastest international goals** in history, netting a goal against **Bhutan** in the **1999 SAF Games** in just **12 seconds**.
 
• **Post-Retirement:** After retiring from professional football, **IM Vijayan** served in the **Kerala Police** and also pursued a career in **acting**, appearing in several **Malayalam films**, including the award-winning movie "Mayaanadhi" and "Shantham".
 
• **AIFF Player of the Year:** This award was started in **1992**, and **IM Vijayan** remains one of the few players to have won it multiple times, showcasing his dominance in the Indian domestic circuit.

questions.question: Which filmmaker returned to the Cannes Film Festival 2025 as a main jury member after winning the Grand Prix in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payal Kapadia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Payal Kapadia** is a distinguished **Indian filmmaker** who achieved international acclaim at the **Cannes Film Festival**.
 
• In **May 2024**, she won the **Grand Prix** at the **77th Cannes Film Festival** for her film **"All We Imagine as Light"**. This was a historic moment as she became the **first Indian filmmaker** ever to win this specific award.
 
• Following her monumental success, she was invited to return to the **78th Cannes Film Festival** in **2025** as a member of the **main Competition jury**.
 
• The **Grand Prix** is considered the **second-most prestigious prize** at the festival, ranking just below the **Palme d'Or**.
 
• Her film, **"All We Imagine as Light"**, was the first **Indian entry** in the **Main Competition** section at Cannes in **30 years**, the last one being **Shaji N. Karun’s "Swaham"** in **1994**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Educational Background**: **Payal Kapadia** is an alumna of the **Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)**, located in **Pune**, where she studied **film direction**.
 
• **Previous Accolades**: Before her 2024 success, she won the **Golden Eye (L'Œil d'or)** for **Best Documentary** at the **2021 Cannes Film Festival** for her work titled **"A Night of Knowing Nothing"**.
 
• **Film Plot**: **"All We Imagine as Light"** is an **Indo-French co-production** that explores the lives of two nurses from **Kerala** working in a nursing home in **Mumbai**, highlighting themes of **urban isolation** and **female bonding**.
 
• **Cannes Film Festival**: Founded in **1946** and held annually in **Cannes, France**, it is one of the most publicized and prestigious film festivals in the world. The **78th edition** is scheduled to take place in **May 2025**.
 
• **Indian Jury Members**: Over the years, several Indian cinema personalities have served on the Cannes jury, including **Mrinal Sen (1982)**, **Mira Nair (1990)**, **Arundhati Roy (2000)**, **Aishwarya Rai (2003)**, **Nandita Das (2005)**, **Sharmila Tagore (2009)**, **Shekhar Kapur (2010)**, **Vidya Balan (2013)**, and **Deepika Padukone (2022)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Award Hierarchy**: In the **Cannes Competition**, the top award is the **Palme d'Or**, followed by the **Grand Prix**, the **Jury Prize**, and individual awards for **Best Director**, **Best Screenplay**, **Best Actress**, and **Best Actor**.
 
• **Significance**: Kapadia's inclusion in the **2025 jury** underscores the **global recognition** of **Indian independent cinema** and its evolving narrative style that resonates with international audiences.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: Her win in **2024** sparked significant discussion regarding the **funding** and **support** for **independent filmmakers** in India, especially those emerging from institutions like **FTII**.

questions.question: What was India’s rank in the Global Innovation Index (GII), 2025, released by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**38th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has achieved the **38th** rank in the **Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025**, marking a significant milestone in its journey toward becoming a global innovation hub. This ranking reflects a steady ascent from its **81st** position in **2015**.
 
• The **Global Innovation Index** is published annually by the **World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)**, a specialized agency of the **United Nations**. It serves as a benchmark for nations to evaluate their innovation ecosystems.
 
• India continues to be the top-ranked economy in the **Central and Southern Asia** region, maintaining its dominance as a leader among **lower-middle-income** economies.
 
• The **2025 report** highlights that India has consistently performed above expectations relative to its **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** per capita for the 15th year in a row, showcasing a high efficiency in converting innovation inputs into outputs.
 
• India’s strengths are particularly visible in indicators such as **ICT services exports**, **venture capital received**, and the quality of its **Science and Engineering graduates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO):**

 
 
• **WIPO** was established in **1967** and is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**. It currently has **193 member states**.
 
• The organization’s mandate is to promote the protection of **intellectual property (IP)** throughout the world through cooperation among states and in collaboration with other international organizations.
 
• It administers **26 international treaties** and provides a global forum for IP services, policy, and information.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Global Innovation Index:**
 
 
• The **GII** framework relies on two sub-indices: the **Innovation Input Sub-Index** and the **Innovation Output Sub-Index**.
 
• The **Innovation Input Sub-Index** is built on five pillars: **Institutions**, **Human Capital and Research**, **Infrastructure**, **Market Sophistication**, and **Business Sophistication**.
 
• The **Innovation Output Sub-Index** is derived from two pillars: **Knowledge and Technology Outputs** and **Creative Outputs**.
 
• The overall score is the average of these two sub-indices, providing a comprehensive view of a nation's **innovation capacity**.
 
 
 
• **India's Innovation Ecosystem:**
 
 
• India's rise in rankings is attributed to government initiatives such as **Startup India**, **Digital India**, and the **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)**.
 
• The country has seen a massive surge in **Unicorn startups** and is home to several major **Science and Technology (S&T) clusters**, including **Bengaluru, Delhi, Chennai, and Mumbai**, which rank among the top 100 clusters globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Innovation Trends:** The **GII 2025** report emphasizes a shift in innovation leadership, with emerging economies in **Asia** closing the gap with traditional leaders in **Europe** and **North America**.
 
• **Intellectual Property Filings:** India has witnessed a record increase in **patent filings**, **trademark registrations**, and **industrial design** applications, which are core metrics monitored by **WIPO**.
 
• **Role of NITI Aayog:** In India, the **NITI Aayog** has been instrumental in tracking the country's performance and has even launched the **India Innovation Index** to foster competitive federalism among states.
 
• **Economic Impact:** Higher innovation rankings are correlated with increased **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** and improved **technological self-reliance**, aligning with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** vision.

questions.question: India’s first-of-its-kind Urban Flood Management Cell (UFMC) powered by Canarys Automations Ltd was inaugurated in which of the following cities in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gorakhpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a significant step towards disaster resilience, **India’s first-of-its-kind Urban Flood Management Cell (UFMC)** was inaugurated in **Gorakhpur**, **Uttar Pradesh**, in **July 2025**.
 
• The **UFMC** is powered by **Canarys Automations Ltd**, a leading **IT** and **automation solutions** provider that specializes in **Hydro-Meteorology** and **Smart City** infrastructure.
 
• This cell is designed to address the critical issue of **urban flooding**, which has increasingly affected major Indian cities due to rapid urbanization and climate change.
 
• The facility integrates high-tech **Internet of Things (IoT)** based monitoring systems that provide **real-time data** on water levels in **drains**, **rivers**, and **low-lying areas** across the city.
 
• The deployment of this cell ensures that the **Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation** and **District Administration** have access to actionable intelligence for immediate intervention during heavy rainfall events. ***Hence, the correct answer is Gorakhpur.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Canarys Automations Ltd:** Based in **Bengaluru**, **Karnataka**, this company has been a pioneer in **automation** and **digital transformation** for over **30 years**. It provides specialized solutions in **telemetry**, **flood forecasting**, and **irrigation automation**.
 
• **Urban Flooding in India:** Unlike riverine floods, **urban flooding** occurs when the **drainage capacity** of a city is overwhelmed by intense rainfall. Cities like **Mumbai**, **Chennai**, and **Bengaluru** have frequently faced this crisis, making the **Gorakhpur** model a potential **national benchmark**.
 
• **Technological Components:** The **UFMC** utilizes **Automatic Rain Gauges (ARG)** and **Automatic Water Level Recorders (AWLR)**. These devices transmit data via **GPRS** or **Satellite** to a central **dashboard** accessible to decision-makers.
 
• **Smart City Mission:** The establishment of such cells often aligns with the **Smart Cities Mission** launched by the **Government of India** in **2015**, which aims to promote sustainable and inclusive cities that provide a decent quality of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Early Warning System (EWS):** The most critical feature of the **Gorakhpur UFMC** is its **Early Warning System**. It can predict potential **inundation** hours in advance, allowing for the **evacuation** of vulnerable populations and the proactive deployment of **water pumps**.
 
• **Gorakhpur’s Geography:** **Gorakhpur** is situated in the **Terai belt** and is prone to flooding from the **Rapti** and **Rohini** rivers. The **UFMC** specifically targets **internal city waterlogging**, which is a major grievance for the **urban population**.
 
• **Data-Driven Governance:** The cell helps in **mapping flood-prone zones** using **GIS (Geographic Information System)**, helping the **urban planners** to improve the **drainage network** for future development.
 
• **Implementation Date:** The project reached its full operational capacity in **July 2025**, coinciding with the peak **monsoon season** in **Northern India**, providing an immediate test for its **predictive capabilities**.

questions.question: Which of the following states became the first to launch the Tribal Genome Sequencing Project in July 2025?

• The project is a landmark initiative by the **Government of Gujarat**, aimed at creating a comprehensive genetic database of the various tribal groups living within the state.

questions.question: Which of the following states activated a 24×7 flood-control room after rivers Subarnarekha, Budhabalanga and Jalaka swelled in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Odisha** state government activated a **24×7 flood-control room** following intensive rainfall that led to the swelling of major rivers in the northern part of the state.
 
• The rivers **Subarnarekha**, **Budhabalanga**, and **Jalaka** reached critical levels, prompting the **Balasore district administration** to initiate emergency protocols to mitigate potential flood damage.
 
• The **Water Resources Department** of **Odisha** deployed technical teams to monitor **river embankments** and ensure that any breaches could be addressed immediately to protect nearby villages.
 
• The **Jalaka river**, in particular, frequently flows above the **danger level** at **Mathani** in the **Basta** block, making it one of the most volatile rivers during the early monsoon season.
 
• The **Special Relief Commissioner (SRC)** of **Odisha** coordinated with the **Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF)** and **Fire Services** to be on high alert for evacuation operations in low-lying areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subarnarekha River**:

 
 
• The **Subarnarekha** (meaning "Streak of Gold") is a multi-state river that flows through **Jharkhand**, **West Bengal**, and **Odisha**.
 
• It originates near **Ranchi** on the **Chota Nagpur Plateau** and has a total length of approximately **395 kilometers** before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• It is a rain-fed river, and its basin covers an area of about **18,951 square kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Budhabalanga River**:
 
 
• This river originates in the **Similipal Biosphere Reserve** in the **Mayurbhanj** district of **Odisha**.
 
• It flows through the districts of **Mayurbhanj** and **Balasore** and has a length of about **175 kilometers**.
 
• The river is famous for the **Barehipani Falls**, which is one of the highest waterfalls in **India**, located within the **Similipal National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Jalaka River**:
 
 
• The **Jalaka** is a smaller but significant river in the **Balasore** district that originates from the **Rasgovindpur** block of **Mayurbhanj**.
 
• It is notorious for causing **flash floods** due to its narrow channel and the heavy siltation that reduces its water-carrying capacity during the **monsoon**.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Management in Odisha**:
 
 
• **Odisha** is considered a leader in disaster management in **India**, having established the **Odisha State Disaster Management Authority (OSDMA)** after the **1999 Super Cyclone**.
 
• The state utilizes the **Early Warning Dissemination System (EWDS)** to alert coastal and riverine populations about incoming natural calamities like **cyclones** and **floods**.
 
• The **Southwest Monsoon** typically enters **Odisha** in the **second or third week of June**, marking the start of the high-risk period for riverine flooding.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Impact**: The northern districts of **Odisha**, including **Balasore**, **Bhadrak**, and **Mayurbhanj**, are highly susceptible to floods because they serve as the drainage point for rivers flowing from the **Chota Nagpur Plateau**.
 
• **Infrastructure**: The state government often utilizes **flood-resilient shelters** and **geospatial mapping** to track the progression of floodwaters in real-time.
 
• **Inter-State Coordination**: Flood management for the **Subarnarekha** often requires coordination between **Odisha** and **Jharkhand** regarding the release of water from the **Galudih Barrage**.

questions.question: Who took office as the Deputy Governor of the RBI on 2 April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poonam Gupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Poonam Gupta** officially took office as the **Deputy Governor** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** on **2 April 2025**.
 
• She was appointed by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)** following the recommendations of the **Financial Sector Regulatory Appointments Search Committee (FSRASC)**.
 
• Her appointment is significant as she transitions from her role as the **Director General** of the **National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER)**, where she was the first woman to lead the institution since its inception in **1956**.
 
• As **Deputy Governor**, she is expected to oversee critical portfolios, likely including the **Monetary Policy Department** and the **Department of Economic and Policy Research**, given her extensive background in macroeconomics.
 
• She succeeds **Michael Debabrata Patra**, who served multiple extended terms as the **Deputy Governor** in charge of monetary policy before his tenure concluded in **2025**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of RBI Leadership**:

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** is governed by a **Central Board of Directors**. The executive leadership consists of one **Governor** and a maximum of **four Deputy Governors**.
 
• The appointments are made under **Section 8** of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The **Governor** and **Deputy Governors** are appointed for a period not exceeding **five years** and are eligible for reappointment.
 
 
 
• **Profile of Poonam Gupta**:
 
 
• Before joining **NCAER**, she served as a **Lead Economist** at the **World Bank** and held positions at the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
• She has been a member of the **Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)**, providing insights on fiscal and monetary health.
 
• Her expertise lies in **international finance**, **banking**, and the **Indian economy**, with numerous publications in global economic journals.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Analysis**:
 
 
• **Michael Debabrata Patra**: Served as **Deputy Governor** from **2020** to **2025**. He was a vital member of the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** and was known for his hawkish stance on inflation.
 
• **Ashwani Bhatia**: A former **Managing Director** of the **State Bank of India (SBI)**, he later served as a **Whole-Time Member (WTM)** at the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**.
 
• **Michael Debroy**: This appears to be a distractor name, potentially conflating **Bibek Debroy** (former Chairman of EAC-PM) and **Michael Patra**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **RBI Headquarters** is located in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**. It was moved from **Kolkata** to **Mumbai** in **1937**.
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** consists of **six members**, including the **Governor** and the **Deputy Governor** in charge of monetary policy, alongside three external members.
 
• The role of the **Deputy Governor** is diverse, ranging from managing the **Foreign Exchange Department** to **Banking Regulation** and **Currency Management** (issuance of **banknotes**).
 
• Historical Significance: While there have been several female **Deputy Governors** in the past (such as **K.J. Udeshi**, **Shyamala Gopinath**, and **Usha Thorat**), the appointment of a specialist from a research background like **Poonam Gupta** continues the tradition of blending lateral entry with internal promotion within the central bank.

questions.question: What are the revised investment caps for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) in corporate bonds for FY 2025-26, as announced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in its move to regulate foreign capital inflows, announced the revised investment caps for **Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs)** for the **fiscal year 2025-26** in **April 2025**.
 
• As per the notification, the limit for **FPI investment** in **corporate bonds** has been maintained at **15%** of the outstanding stock of corporate bonds.
 
• This limit is part of the **Medium-Term Framework (MTF)**, which aims to provide a predictable regime for foreign investment in the Indian debt market while ensuring financial stability.
 
• The **RBI** keeps these limits under review to balance the need for attracting **foreign exchange** and managing the volatility associated with **portfolio flows**.
 
• These regulations apply to all **FPIs** registered with the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)**, ensuring that the total holdings of all foreign investors do not exceed the specified **15%** threshold of the total market value of outstanding corporate debt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI):** 
 
 
• **FPI** refers to the entry of funds into a country where foreigners deposit money in a country's **bank** or make purchases in the country's **stock and bond markets**.
 
• Unlike **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, FPI does not provide the investor with direct control over the assets or the management of the companies.
 
 
 
• **Corporate Bonds:** 
 
 
• These are **debt instruments** issued by private and public corporations to raise **capital** for various purposes, such as business expansion or refinancing existing debt.
 
• In India, the **corporate bond market** is a crucial source of funding for infrastructure and industrial projects, and **FPI participation** provides necessary **liquidity** to this market.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Authority:** 
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** jointly manage the framework for foreign investments.
 
• The **RBI** determines the macro-prudential limits (the caps), while **SEBI** manages the registration and operational guidelines for the investors.
 
 
 
• **Voluntary Retention Route (VRR):** 
 
 
• The **VRR** is a separate channel introduced by the **RBI** to encourage FPIs to invest in **debt markets** in India over a longer period.
 
• Investments through **VRR** are exempt from certain regulatory prescriptions, provided the investors voluntarily commit to retaining a required minimum percentage of their **investment** in India for a specific period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Securities (G-Secs):** Apart from corporate bonds, the **RBI** also sets limits for **G-Secs**. Historically, the limit for FPIs in **Central Government Securities** has been around **6%** of the outstanding stock, which is significantly lower than the **15%** allowed for corporate debt.
 
• **State Development Loans (SDLs):** For **SDLs**, the investment limit is typically set at **2%** of the outstanding stock.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** A **15%** cap helps in deepening the **debt market** without making it overly dependent on foreign "hot money," which can be pulled out quickly during global financial crises, leading to **currency depreciation**.
 
• **Fully Accessible Route (FAR):** Certain specified categories of **Government Securities** are opened fully for FPIs without any macro-prudential caps under the **FAR** scheme, which was a major step towards India's inclusion in **global bond indices**.

questions.question: In May 2025, minutes after the PSLV-C61, carrying the earth observation satellite EOS-09, lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, the space agency reported a glitch in the _____.

options.text: third stage of the launch vehicle
second stage of the launch vehicle
fourth stage of the launch vehicle
first stage of the launch vehicle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**third stage of the launch vehicle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **PSLV-C61** mission, launched in **May 2025**, was intended to place the **EOS-09** satellite into its designated **Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit**.
 
• Shortly after a successful lift-off from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)** in **Sriharikota**, **ISRO** (Indian Space Research Organisation) identified a technical glitch specifically in the **third stage (PS3)** of the launch vehicle. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The **third stage** of the **PSLV** is critical as it utilizes a **solid rocket motor** to provide the necessary thrust after the vehicle has exited the denser layers of the **Earth's atmosphere**.
 
• Preliminary reports indicated that the anomaly occurred during the **ignition** or **burn phase** of this stage, which hindered the vehicle's ability to reach the required **velocity** for the next phase of the mission.
 
• While the **first** and **second stages** performed nominally, the failure in the **third stage** prevented the **fourth stage** from executing the final **orbital injection**. ***Hence, options 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) Structure**:

 
 
• **First Stage (PS1)**: This stage uses a **solid propellant (HTPB)** and is augmented by **strap-on boosters** to provide massive initial thrust.
 
• **Second Stage (PS2)**: This stage employs the **Vikas Engine**, which uses **liquid propellants** (UH25 and N2O4).
 
• **Third Stage (PS3)**: A **solid motor** stage that provides high thrust at high altitudes. It is designed to operate in a **vacuum**.
 
• **Fourth Stage (PS4)**: The uppermost stage of the **PSLV**, comprising two **liquid engines** that are **restartable** to ensure precise satellite placement.
 
 
 
• **EOS-09 (Earth Observation Satellite)**:
 
 
• The **EOS-09** is a high-resolution **imaging satellite** designed for **Earth observation**.
 
• Its primary **applications** include **urban planning**, **agriculture monitoring**, **forestry management**, and **disaster mitigation**.
 
• It was equipped with advanced **optical sensors** to provide data for **cartographic** and **oceanographic** studies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)**: Located in **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**, it is India’s primary **spaceport** responsible for launching **PSLV**, **GSLV**, and **LVM3** missions.
 
• **PSLV Glitches**: Though known as the **Workhorse of ISRO** due to its high success rate, the **PSLV** has occasionally faced challenges, such as the **PSLV-C39** mission failure (heat shield separation issue) and early developmental flight anomalies.
 
• **Mission Analysis**: In the event of a **third-stage glitch**, a **Failure Analysis Committee (FAC)** is typically formed by **ISRO** to investigate the **telemetry data** and identify the root cause, such as **pressure drops** or **propellant exhaustion**.
 
• **Significance of May 2025**: This mission was part of **India's** ongoing effort to enhance its **space-based surveillance** and **remote sensing** capabilities.

questions.question: Who among the following won the Laureus World Action Sportsperson of the Year award in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tom Pidcock**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tom Pidcock** has been honored with the **Laureus World Action Sportsperson of the Year** award in **2025**, recognizing his extraordinary achievements in the field of extreme and action sports during the previous calendar year.
 
• The **British** cyclist secured this prestigious title primarily due to his spectacular performance at the **2024 Paris Olympics**, where he won the **Gold Medal** in the **Men’s Cross-country Mountain Bike** event despite suffering a mid-race puncture.
 
• **Tom Pidcock** is widely regarded as one of the most versatile athletes in modern cycling, competing at the highest level in **Mountain Biking**, **Road Cycling**, and **Cyclo-cross**.
 
• He represents the **INEOS Grenadiers** professional cycling team and has previously won major titles such as the **Olympic Gold** in **Tokyo 2020** and the **Cyclo-cross World Championship** in **2022**.
 
• This award marks a significant milestone as he becomes one of the few cyclists to be recognized in the **Action Sportsperson** category, which is typically dominated by sports like surfing, skating, and snowboarding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Laureus World Sports Awards:**
 
 
• Established in **1999** by the **Laureus Sport for Good Foundation**, these awards are often described as the “Oscars of Sports.”
 
• The awards ceremony honors individuals and teams for their sporting achievements throughout the **year**.
 
 
 
• **Other Nominees and Profiles:**
 
 
• **Yuto Horigome:** A **Japanese** professional **skateboarder** who made history by winning the first-ever **Olympic Gold Medal** in the men's street event at the **2020 Tokyo Games** and defended it at the **2024 Paris Games**.
 
• **Kelly Slater:** An **American** professional **surfer** who is an **11-time World Surf League champion**. He is considered the greatest professional surfer of all time, holding records for both the youngest and oldest world champion.
 
• **Chloe Kim:** An **American** **snowboarder** and **two-time Olympic Gold Medalist**. She became the youngest woman to win an Olympic snowboarding gold medal at the **2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics** at the **age** of **17**.
 
 
 
• **Tom Pidcock’s Notable Achievements:**
 
 
• Born in **July 1999** in **Leeds, United Kingdom**.
 
• Won the iconic **Alpe d'Huez** stage of the **Tour de France** in **2022**, becoming the youngest rider ever to win on that specific climb.
 
• He holds **World Championship** titles across multiple disciplines, showcasing his unique **functions** and **applications** of skill in diverse cycling terrains.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Laureus World Action Sportsperson of the Year** category specifically focuses on **non-traditional** sports that involve high levels of risk and physical dexterity.
 
• The selection process involves a two-step system: a **Nominations Panel** of the world’s leading sports editors, writers, and broadcasters votes to create a shortlist, and then the **Laureus World Sports Academy** members (sporting legends) vote for the winners by secret ballot.
 
• The **2025** awards highlighted the **features** of resilience and mental strength, epitomized by **Tom Pidcock’s** recovery from a **30-second** deficit during his **Olympic** race in **Paris**.
 
• Other major categories at the **Laureus Awards** include **World Sportsman of the Year**, **World Sportswoman of the Year**, **World Team of the Year**, and **Breakthrough of the Year**.

questions.question: In August 2025, Union Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava, virtually inaugurated an innovative national mechanism aimed at evaluating and improving state drug regulatory frameworks through an open and evidence-based approach named ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Health Regulatory Excellence Index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the **Union Health Secretary**, **Punya Salila Srivastava**, inaugurated a significant national mechanism known as the **State Health Regulatory Excellence Index**.
 
• This index is designed as a strategic tool to **evaluate and improve state drug regulatory frameworks** across India. It focuses on creating a competitive yet collaborative environment for states to enhance their oversight of the **pharmaceutical sector**.
 
• The mechanism follows an **open and evidence-based approach**, ensuring that the performance of **State Drug Controller** offices is measured against standardized **benchmarks** and **data-driven metrics**.
 
• The primary objective of the index is to achieve **regulatory harmonization**, which is essential for maintaining the **safety, efficacy, and quality** of **medical products** manufactured and distributed within the country.
 
• By identifying specific gaps in the **regulatory ecosystem**, the index encourages **State Governments** to invest in **human resources**, **testing laboratories**, and **digital infrastructure** to meet international standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO):**

 
 
• The **CDSCO** is the **National Regulatory Authority (NRA)** of India under the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**.
 
• It works in coordination with **State Drug Regulatory Authorities** to enforce the **Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940** and the **Rules, 1945**.
 
• The **Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI)** heads the **CDSCO** and is responsible for the approval of **new drugs** and **clinical trials**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework in India:**
 
 
• The **pharmaceutical industry** in India is the **3rd largest** in the world by volume. To sustain this, robust **compliance monitoring** is required.
 
• The **State Health Regulatory Excellence Index** acts as a catalyst for **Ease of Doing Business** by streamlining the **licensing process** and reducing **administrative bottlenecks**.
 
• It promotes the adoption of **Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)** and **Good Distribution Practices** among small and medium enterprises (**SMEs**).
 
 
 
• **Pharmaceutical Compliance:**
 
 
• Maintaining **Global Supply Chain** integrity requires strict adherence to **quality control** protocols.
 
• The index monitors parameters such as the **number of inspections** conducted, the **sampling of drugs** for testing, and the **prosecution of offenders** dealing in **spurious or sub-standard drugs**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evidence-Based Evaluation:** The index utilizes **real-time data** from **integrated portals** to minimize manual errors and enhance **transparency** in reporting.
 
• **Capacity Building:** One of the critical outcomes of this initiative is the **training and development** of **Drug Inspectors** to handle complex **biotechnology** and **medical device** regulations.
 
• **Public Health Impact:** By strengthening the **regulatory frameworks**, the **Government of India** aims to bolster **public trust** in the **healthcare system** and ensure that every citizen has access to **safe and affordable medicines**.
 
• **Viksit Bharat 2047:** This initiative is a part of the broader vision to make India a **global leader** in **healthcare innovation** and **pharmaceutical manufacturing** by the **centenary of independence**.

questions.question: The Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2025, conducted in November 2025, was held in __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2025** was officially convened in **New Delhi** during the month of **November 2025**.
 
• This high-level conclave serves as a strategic platform for **policymakers**, **scientists**, **industry leaders**, and **academicians** to deliberate on the future of India's scientific landscape.
 
• The primary focus of the **ESTIC 2025** was to foster a collaborative ecosystem for **deep-tech startups** and to accelerate the commercialization of homegrown technologies.
 
• During the event, several sessions were dedicated to the integration of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Quantum Computing**, and **Biotechnology** into the national mainstream to drive economic growth.
 
• The venue, **New Delhi**, was chosen due to its status as the administrative hub where key decisions regarding the **National Science and Technology Policy** are formulated and implemented.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of New Delhi in Innovation:**

 
 
• As the capital city, **New Delhi** hosts major research institutions such as the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT Delhi)** and the headquarters of the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)**.
 
• The city acts as the primary link between **government ministries** and **international scientific delegations**, making it the ideal location for global conclaves like **ESTIC**.
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas of ESTIC 2025:**
 
 
• **Quantum Technology:** Discussions centered on the **National Quantum Mission (NQM)**, aiming to make India a global leader in quantum communication and sensing by **2031**.
 
• **Green Energy:** The conclave highlighted innovations in **Green Hydrogen** and **Solid-state Batteries** to meet the **Net Zero** targets by **2070**.
 
• **Digital Infrastructure:** Strengthening the **India Stack** and expanding **6G technology** research were key highlights of the technological roadmap discussed during the event.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives Supporting Innovation:**
 
 
• The **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)**, established to seed and promote research across universities, played a pivotal role in the themes of the **2025 conclave**.
 
• India’s consistent rise in the **Global Innovation Index (GII)**, where it moved from the **81st rank in 2015** to within the **top 40** in recent years, provided the backdrop for the high optimism at the event.
 
• The **Startup India** initiative has also been a major contributor, with India now hosting over **100 unicorns**, many of which are in the **science and technology** sectors.
 
 
 
• **Future Outlook:**
 
 
• The conclave emphasized the vision of **Viksit Bharat @2047**, where **Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI)** will be the cornerstones of a developed Indian economy.
 
• Emphasis was placed on **IPR (Intellectual Property Rights)** awareness to ensure that **Indian innovations** are protected and incentivized on a global scale.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dates and Venue:** The event was specifically held in **November 2025** at a prominent convention center in **New Delhi**.
 
• **Technology Missions:** A major part of the conclave was the review of the **National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS)**.
 
• **Collaborations:** High-level MoUs between **Indian startups** and **Global Tech Firms** were signed to enhance the **manufacturing of semiconductors** within the country under the **India Semiconductor Mission**.
 
• **Sustainability:** The **ESTIC 2025** conclave itself adopted **eco-friendly practices**, showcasing a commitment to the **Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE)** movement.

questions.question: India joined which European drone programme as an observer in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eurodrone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, **India** officially joined the **Eurodrone** program as an **observer**, marking a significant expansion of its defense cooperation with **European** nations.
 
• The **Eurodrone** is a collaborative project between **Germany**, **France**, **Italy**, and **Spain**, designed to develop an advanced **Medium-Altitude Long-Endurance (MALE)** Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (**RPAS**).
 
• The program is managed by **OCCAR** (Organisation for Joint Armament Co-operation), which acts as the executive agent on behalf of the participating **European** member states.
 
• As an **observer**, **India** will have the opportunity to participate in technical briefings, track the progress of **aerospace** development, and understand the technical standards required for **unmanned aerial systems** in **non-segregated airspace**.
 
• This move is seen as a strategic step for **India** to diversify its **surveillance** and **reconnaissance** capabilities while strengthening the **India-EU** defense and security partnership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technical Specifications of Eurodrone:**

 
 
• The **Eurodrone** is notable for its **twin-turboprop engine** configuration, which provides enhanced safety and reliability compared to single-engine platforms.
 
• It is designed for multi-mission capabilities, including **Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition, and Reconnaissance (ISTAR)**, as well as potential future **combat** applications.
 
• Key industrial partners involved in the project include **Airbus Defence and Space**, **Dassault Aviation**, and **Leonardo**.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance for India:**
 
 
• India's **Ministry of Defence** aims to reduce dependence on any single source for **HALE** and **MALE** drones. Currently, India utilizes **Heron** drones from **Israel** and is in the process of inducting **MQ-9B Predator** drones from the **USA**.
 
• The **observer status** allows **DRDO** and Indian **aerospace** experts to gain insights into **European** digital design and manufacturing processes, which could benefit indigenous projects like **TAPAS-BH-201**.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Options:**
 
 
• **nEUROn**: This is an experimental **unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV)** developed by **Dassault Aviation** focused on **stealth** technology.
 
• **Global Hawk**: A **High-Altitude Long-Endurance (HALE)** platform produced by **Northrop Grumman** in the **United States**.
 
• **Predator XP**: An export variant of the **MQ-1 Predator** drone manufactured by **General Atomics**; it is an older generation system compared to the current **MQ-9B** series.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Eurodrone** program officially entered its contract phase in **2022**, with the first flight originally targeted for the **late 2020s**.
 
• **India's** inclusion as an **observer** follows high-level **diplomatic** engagements and **security** dialogues held in **New Delhi** and **Brussels** during **2024**.
 
• Participation in such programs is essential for **India** to ensure that its future **RPAS** fleets are interoperable with international **air traffic management** standards, allowing them to fly in civilian **airspace** without specific restrictions.
 
• The **India-EU** roadmap for **2025** emphasizes cooperation in **cutting-edge technology**, and the **Eurodrone** observer status is a tangible outcome of this **policy** framework.

• The **Asian Wrestling Championships 2025** was held in **Amman, Jordan**, during **April 2025**, featuring elite wrestlers from across the continent including powerhouses like **Japan** and **Kyrgyzstan**.
